I've farmed these 16.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. It's just me and my wife now — our children work in the city — so every decision has to balance our backs against the bills. We grow wheat-maize double cropping on the whole plot; it's the only system that keeps food on the table and leaves a little cash for medicine and repairs. My well gives reliable water, but electricity for pumping is expensive, so I count every irrigation carefully.

It's early spring. My wheat went in last October with an improved variety, and I already gave it base fertilizer and winter irrigation before the freeze. Now I need to carry it through to harvest in June. I'll topdress about 10 kg of urea per mu when the wheat greens up, then irrigate three times: at green-up, at jointing, and once during grain filling. Three is enough — a fourth would cost too much in power and my old shoulders can't haul those pipes around again. I'll spray herbicide once when the weeds appear, and watch for aphids; if they show up, I'll spray insecticide too. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the spring rains don't fail us.

After wheat harvest in early June, the window is brutally short. I'll hire my nephew's tractor for rotary tillage right away — bury the wheat stubble and get a clean seedbed — then plant hybrid maize seed. I never save maize seed; hybrids lose vigor. I'll put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea at big trumpet stage, totaling about 15 kg nitrogen per mu. For maize, two irrigations: one at jointing and one at tasseling. That's when the water really pays. I'll spray herbicide after emergence and insecticide for corn borer. I'm hoping for 580 kg per mu. I don't chase every last kilogram anymore — I'm 62, and 580 pays the bills without breaking me.
